Knowledge recorded by Shinnecock elders in 2014

Knobbed and channeled whelks

Whelks supplied food, shell ornaments, and whistles. The catalogue describes the spiral as a useful material and connects shells with agricultural work. It distinguishes knobbed and channeled shells while recording their shared cultural uses.1

Places named in the catalogue

Long Island Sound; Atlantic Ocean; Shinnecock Bay; Mecox Bay; Montauk Bay; Peconic Bay; Napeague Bay.1

Page references

The Shinnecock Environmental Department compiled this catalogue from elders’ memories and community resource knowledge in 2014. Food and medicine appear here as historical knowledge; safe identification and treatment require current guidance.

Shinnecock Environmental Department, Natural Resources Identified by Shinnecock Elders, April 4, 2014, PDF pp. 5–6. Page numbers count the cover as PDF page 1.
